title: The work behind your presence.
intro: Start with one part or agree a broader programme. Each has a clear output and a review.

profile.headline: Make your profile clear.
profile.why: Align your headline, About section and featured work with the buyer and the product.
profile.check: Ask a new reader who you help and what you do.

strategy.headline: Give content a direction.
strategy.why: Connect buyer questions to product decisions, founder experience and evidence. Turn the themes into a working calendar.
strategy.check: Each theme has a buyer question and a source.

writing.headline: Keep the founder’s voice.
writing.why: Interviews supply the material. Drafts keep the founder’s judgment and technical meaning open to review.
writing.check: Read the draft aloud and check each claim.

design.headline: Show how the product works.
design.why: Use carousels, diagrams and video to explain the decisions and ideas behind the business.
design.check: A reader can explain the idea after seeing the visual.

automation.headline: Keep the work moving.
automation.why: Organise sources, drafts and approvals in one agreed workflow. Automate repeatable administration where appropriate.
automation.check: Every step has an owner and an approval.

marketing.headline: Prepare the next conversation.
marketing.why: Align founder and company messages with manual outreach starters and follow-up copy for an agreed buyer.
marketing.check: Each message has a relevant reason to contact.

advertising.headline: Test the message with paid media.
advertising.why: Develop an audience, creative and landing-page brief around an agreed objective and test budget.
advertising.check: The plan names the audience, objective and review point.

measurement.headline: Use evidence to choose the next test.
measurement.why: Review authorised engagement, qualified replies and attributed leads separately. Report what the available data can support.
measurement.check: Each measure has a source, period and decision.

definition.label: In short
definition.question: What is founder-led LinkedIn marketing?
definition.answer: Founder-led LinkedIn marketing turns a founder’s experience and product decisions into a clear profile and content for their intended buyers. Outspoken supports the strategy, writing and visual work; the founder reviews the claims.
